differences.what: roof: the engraving's mansard, its steep lower faces bowed a little to a curb about 2.9 m over the cornice, under a low upper hip; the build's was a 30-degree tin hip
wall head: the engraving's cornice stands about 8.2 m over grade (its soffit 7.9 m); the build's walls stood 0.7 m higher

north pavilion: the north 3.75 m of the front (v 7.5-11.25) is a pavilion standing a little proud, with two round-headed windows a storey under moulded hoods and a light corner strip at its north corner; the build's front is flat there and carries the canted bay
crown: over the pavilion a taller bell-curved mansard with one round-headed dormer, rising about 0.7 m over the main curb; the build has none
corner strip: the engraving draws a light strip down the pavilion's north corner, a stone or painted quoin; T-2404's pavilion turns that corner in its own brick
dormers: round-headed dormers in the mansard's lower face, two seen on the north face; the build's mansard has none
bay window: a one-storey bay on the SOUTH part of the front (about v 0.5-4.4) under a flared, bracketed hood with a finial; the build's bay is two storeys on the north part

windows: round-headed sash under moulded hoods on the street front; an upper window over the bay with an ornate head; the north wall's windows flat-headed, two a storey toward the front; the build's are flat-headed two-over-two under segmental brick arches, three on the north wall

entrance: the door at about v 5-6.6 under a hood, reached by a stoop rising north along the front to a porch with a turned balustrade before the pavilion; the build's door is at v 1.9 at the head of a straight stoop

fence: a lattice of interlaced pointed arches on a solid base along the street line, a board fence on the north side; the build's is the K11 scroll-band iron fence on a stone curb with stone gate piers and urns
chimney: a tall stack at the front of the north wall, rising from the cornice beside the crown; the build's two stacks stand on the ridge
roof covering: the lower faces read as slate in courses; the build's is painted standing-seam tin (K04 slates nothing under 25 degrees, and the upper hip is 18)

walls' tone: the engraving draws the front light and the north wall and the pavilion's north half dark, its light from the south-east; the house's colour (the Inter Ocean's 'olive green' of 1887) and its walling are not shown in a monochrome print
the south side wall and the rear: the engraving sees neither

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
